description: KEPT AS A FLOOR (decision recorded on #49, 2026-07-25): this static rule is no longer the primary grade-quality detector - dashboards/alert-grade-quality-anomaly.json (seasonal anomaly rule on correct-decision volume) is now primary, because a fixed 50% floor is a poor detector against a baseline that moves with the model roster (~58.8% lifetime, not fixed). This rule stays wired up anyway, for two reasons an anomaly rule cannot cover by itself: (1) cold start / thin baseline - the anomaly rule needs several days-to-weeks of seasonal history to score meaningfully, and has none yet in this hackathon-era deployment; a coin-flip-or-worse floor is meaningful from evaluation one. (2) boiling-frog drift - an anomaly rule detects deviation from ITS OWN recent history, so a slow multi-day decline could get normalized into the seasonal baseline and never register as anomalous, while an absolute floor never moves. Original rationale, unchanged: fires when the correct-decision rate (count(correct) / count(all), filtered to augmentloop.grade.source in math+reality per ADR 0001 - ai_judge grades never count toward this either) drops below 50% over a rolling 30-minute window. Baseline: lifetime accumulated rate across toy-world test runs is ~58.8% (10/17 correct). 50% is below coin-flip performance for a route/quote-extraction decision the engine can grade objectively, catching a real quality regression (e.g. a right-sizing reroute to a cheaper model that silently broke correctness). Query note: this rule's 30-minute evalWindow is comfortably inside the increase()/rate() working range verified on #49/#50 (real data up to ~3h, silently null at 6h+), so unlike the channel-routing gap this rule's query itself was never the problem.
